sections.h2: Who handles property tax inside the Todd County courthouse?
sections.html:
Todd County puts its tax work in one building: the courthouse at 202 East Washington Street in Elkton. All three offices answer through the county switchboard at (270) 265-9966, each on its own extension.

  • Sheriff, ext. 208: takes payment of property tax bills. The sheriff's website lets owners view their bills online and says payment cannot be made there, so ask the office which payment methods it accepts.
  • Property Valuation Administration (PVA), ext. 504: the county's answer for the value of a property and for disputing that value.
  • County clerk, ext. 501: registers vehicles and, after April 15, runs the delinquent-tax process.

The City of Elkton keeps a separate property tax payment link on its own website. If your address is inside the city, ask the city whether a city bill exists in addition to the county bill.

sections.h2: What sets Todd County apart from the counties around it?
sections.html:
Todd County spans 377 square miles and almost none of it is water, 2.6 square miles in all. The legislature created it on April 1, 1820, from parts of Christian and Logan counties, after residents petitioned for a seat of government closer than the two existing ones. It was named for Colonel John Todd, killed at the Battle of Blue Licks in 1782.

Historically the county divides into a northern high country of steep sandstone slopes with oak, walnut and poplar, and a southern low country of rolling limestone flatlands. The lowlands, with Pembroke soil, are known for strong crop yields, and farming is a long-standing local tradition. In the early 1800s a stagecoach hub at what is now Guthrie sent routes out to larger cities. Elkton took its name from the elk that watered at a spring near the center of town, and its courthouse square was laid out as a trapezoid rather than a square, so buildings on both sides catch sunlight longer.

The cities are Elkton, Guthrie and Trenton, with Allensville and Fairview (mostly in Christian County) as census-designated places. Muhlenberg, Logan and Christian counties border Todd, as do Robertson and Montgomery counties in Tennessee. Todd County runs on Central time and has a single public school district, the Todd County School District, with Todd County Central High School.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures say about Todd County homes?
sections.html:
Todd County had 12,972 residents in July 2025, up 5.9 percent from the 2020 base after a small dip in the 2020 count. For a seller, the housing numbers matter most:

  • The median owner-occupied home is valued at $166,700, the lowest of the four counties in this set.
  • 76.0 percent of homes are owner-occupied, among 4,559 households.
  • Median gross rent is $851, higher than in Taylor and Trigg counties.
  • The county had 5,313 housing units in 2025 and 40 building permits.
  • Median household income is $61,103, and the mean commute is 27.8 minutes.

The 2020 census recorded 10.8 percent of housing units as vacant and 30.0 percent of occupied homes as rented. Retail sales in 2022 came to $150.3 million.

sections.h2: When do Todd County property tax bills go delinquent?
sections.html:
Kentucky law sets the calendar, and Todd County follows it. Under the regular schedule a bill is due by December 31 of the assessment year. Paying by November 1 saves 2 percent, a payment between November 2 and December 31 owes only the face amount, and paying in January adds 5 percent. After January 31 the penalty is 10 percent, plus the sheriff's add-on fee.

At the close of business on April 15, the sheriff hands every unpaid bill to the county clerk. A lien is recorded against the property, and the bill is then called a certificate of delinquency. Interest of 1 percent per month starts, and the clerk, county attorney and recording fees follow.

sections.h2: How much does a Todd County delinquent bill cost over time?
sections.html:
The Department of Revenue publishes a worked example for a bill with a $1,000 face amount, assuming a 4 percent sheriff's commission. The same pattern applies to a Todd County certificate, though the actual commission rates come from the local offices.

Illustrative cost of a $1,000 delinquent bill at each stage (source: Kentucky Department of Revenue worked example)
StageTotal due
Certificate when it reaches the clerk$1,254.00
Paid within five business days$1,387.79
Paid after the county attorney's first notice$1,611.30
Paid in May, second month of interest$1,627.61
Paid in June after advertising$1,659.90
Amount a third-party purchaser pays at the sale$1,704.21

Waiting adds money quickly, and the county attorney's fee is waived only when the owner pays inside the first five business days. Once a purchaser buys the certificate, the lien is assigned to that company and the owner pays the purchaser.

sections.h2: When does the Todd County tax sale happen?
sections.html:
State law puts the sale 90 to 135 days after bills reach the clerk, which for a regular schedule means a date between July 14 and August 28. The county clerk publishes the dates for each year in order: a half-page advertisement, the advertisement of the full list, the deadline for third-party registration, and finally the sale, which starts at 9 AM.

Buyers who want up to three bills register with the county. Anyone buying more than three registers with the state instead. The clerk's page notes that buying a tax bill does not mean the purchaser owns the property, only that a lien is placed on it. Before the sale, the county attorney mails a 30-day notice and, if needed, a second notice within 60 days, and the delinquent list must run in the local newspaper 30 to 45 days ahead of the sale.

sections.h2: What is the process for disputing a Todd County assessment?
sections.html:
The county FAQ sends valuation disputes to the PVA in the courthouse. A conference is a required first step. The tax roll then lies open for thirteen days beginning the first Monday in May, and a written appeal must reach the county clerk by the close of business on the day after the period ends.

The local board of assessment appeals meets 25 to 35 days later for no more than five days. It looks for evidence such as comparable sales, an appraisal, cost of construction or insurance records, and it rejects appeals that lack them. Missing the local board means no later review by the Kentucky Claims Commission. A person paid to speak for the owner must be a professional such as an attorney, accountant, broker or appraiser, and must carry written authorization.

sections.h2: Does Todd County have a homestead exemption, and how does it affect a sale?
sections.html:
Kentucky's homestead exemption applies in Todd County for owners at least 65 or totally disabled. The Department of Revenue set the deduction at $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, and the application goes to the Todd County PVA by December 31. Because the benefit belongs to the owner, a buyer must apply again.

When selling, request a payoff from the sheriff and ask the clerk about any older certificate. Kentucky treats each year's tax as the personal debt of the owner on January 1, and a delinquent lien stays with the property for up to eleven years, so the closing agent should see a clean record before funds are released.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Todd County property taxes?
faqs.a: Pay at the Todd County Sheriff's Office, 202 East Washington Street inside the courthouse, or call (270) 265-9966 ext. 208. The sheriff's website shows bills online, so confirm with the office how payments are accepted.

faqs.q: Who do I call if my Todd County assessment seems wrong?
faqs.a: Call the PVA at (270) 265-9966 ext. 504 and request a conference. That meeting is required before any appeal can go to the local board of assessment appeals.

faqs.q: What is the Todd County homestead exemption amount?
faqs.a: It is $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 tax periods. Owners must be 65 or older, or totally disabled, and apply with the PVA before December 31.

faqs.q: Can a company buy my overdue Todd County tax bill?
faqs.a: Yes. After April 15 the bill sits with the clerk, and a third-party purchaser can buy it at the annual sale. That company then holds the lien and collects from you.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Todd County house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as the amount owed is paid from the sale. Ask the sheriff and the clerk for written payoffs so no certificate surprises the buyer's closing agent.
